title: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
authors: Zepeng Wang, Jason Phang, Harsh Jhamtani, Siva Reddy
abstract: We introduce SciMON, a system for generating novel scientific ideas by retrieving relevant scientific literature and iteratively refining proposals to optimize novelty. While retrieval provides relevant inspirations, flat vector retrieval often retrieves redundant papers and fails to capture relational and structural cross-paper connections, leading to noisy contexts and repetitive suggestions.

title: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation through Multi-Agent Collaboration
authors: Jie Tang, Lei Xia, Ziyi Li, Chao Huang
abstract: We present AI-Researcher, an autonomous multi-agent framework where specialized LLM agents collaborate to conduct literature review, generate hypotheses, and design experiments. Despite multi-agent debating mechanisms, the system incurs high token expenditure and lacks topological citation graph grounding to verify the empirical boundaries of proposed research gaps.

title: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
authors: Boci Peng, Yun Zhu, Yong Liu, Xiaohe Bo, Haoran Deng
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language models by integrating external knowledge. Graph RAG organizes retrieved knowledge as relational graphs rather than flat document chunks. However, constructing knowledge graphs from raw academic abstracts often produces sparse and heterogeneous relation matrices that require topological regularization.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandara Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin
abstract: Large pre-trained language models store factual knowledge in their parameters, but their ability to access and manipulate knowledge is limited. We explore general-purpose fine-tuning recipes for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), combining pre-trained parametric memory with non-parametric neural retrieval via Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR). Flat text passages lack multi-hop cross-document reasoning capabilities.
